title: Status controversiae: Protestants reject all such cult as superstition; Rome affirms it under anathema and solemn praxis
source_text: XII. Omnem vero ejusmodi cultum, quocunque tandem nomine vocetur, Protestantes communi consensu rejiciunt, ut superstitiosum, & verbo Dei contrarium. Atque in eo consistit hujus controversiae status, inter Ecclesiam Romanam, & Protestantium Ecclesias omnes, An, scilicet, pium sit, Deoque gratum & acceptum, coram imaginibus, vel Christi, vel Sanctorum, procumbere, caput aperire, incensum adolere, cereos accendere, & ritus alios similes exercere religionis ergo? Quod uno ore negant Protestantes, affirmant vero Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae tanquam aliquid ab Ecclesia sua sub anathemate sancitum, & solenni ac universali praxi illius confirmatum.
pass_a_gloss: But every cult of that kind, by whatever name finally it be called, the Protestants by common consent reject, as superstitious, and contrary to the word of God. And in that consists the status of this controversy, between the Roman Church, and all the Churches of the Protestants, Whether, namely, it is pious, and pleasing and acceptable to God, before images, either of Christ, or of the Saints, to prostrate, to uncover the head, to burn incense, to light candles, and to exercise other like rites for religion’s sake? Which with one mouth the Protestants deny, but the Doctors of the Roman Church affirm as something sanctioned by their Church under anathema, and confirmed by her solemn and universal praxis.
pass_b_english: Protestants with one mouth refuse every such rite as superstition against God’s word.
The quarrel’s status is simply whether kneeling, bare head, incense, and candles before images please God—Rome says yes under anathema and universal praxis.

choices.why: Protestant censure of the whole praxis.
